title: The Tollhouse Ledger
description: A short quest sequence — three factions want the same hidden ledger. The player decides who wins.

storyboards.title: Quest 01: The Ruined Tollhouse
storyboards.description: The player arrives at a war-scarred tollhouse and discovers a document that could change the region's balance of power.

frames.title: The Caravan Arrives Damaged
frames.summary: The road through the Ashmarrow Pass is silent. A merchant caravan sits abandoned outside a ruined tollhouse. No guards. No travelers.

content.designerNotes: Open with environmental storytelling: old smoke smell, wagon wheels cracked but not looted (strange detail — rewards observant players), silence where road noise should be. The caravan belongs to the Dalthor trading house — surface this through markings, not dialogue.
content.playerVisibleText: The merchant road through the pass should be busy at this hour. It isn't. A caravan has stopped outside a half-collapsed tollhouse and no one is moving.
authorOnlyNotes: The caravan wasn't attacked — the merchants fled voluntarily after one of them glimpsed the ledger inside the tollhouse and recognized what it was.
A Velthari courier is watching from the treeline. She won't act yet — do not surface her until the encounter beat.
involvedCharacters: Marel Dyn (fleeing merchant, will give backstory if calmed)
content.stakes: Establishing atmosphere and the first hook — something is wrong here that isn't just bandits.
entryConditions: Player has entered the Ashmarrow Pass zone
exitConditions: Player has entered the tollhouse interior OR spoken to Marel Dyn
stateChanges: Sets: caravan_owner = dalthor (queryable by subsequent beats)

Ruined tollhouse exterior — collapsed section, smoke staining
Abandoned Dalthor caravan — wagons with house markings, cracked wheels (not looted)
Merchant NPC Marel Dyn — hiding state, calmed-state dialogue variant
Courier Savan Vreil treeline placement — invisible trigger volume, no visual
Environmental audio: road silence, distant bird, absence of traffic

Three distinct readable environmental details present in tollhouse approach area

Implement Marel Dyn as a discoverable NPC with two-sentence backstory dialogue
Place courier Savan in the treeline — invisible until the encounter beat triggers

annotations.text: Do not place bodies here. The silence is more unsettling than carnage — design for absence, not violence.
Target 5–8 minutes of play time. Establish the wrongness and push toward the tollkeeper.

frames.title: The Wounded Tollkeeper
frames.summary: Inside the tollhouse, old Orvyn Kett is hiding under the counter with a crossbow bolt in his shoulder and a story he doesn't want to tell.

content.designerNotes: Orvyn is terrified but not stupid. Design his dialogue tree to close off if the player uses aggressive dialogue options. He opens up in response to calm, competent approaches — healing him, acknowledging the threat, speaking quietly. He knows what the ledger is but not the full scope of what it proves. He knows three different factions came asking for it in the last two days.
content.playerVisibleText: A stout old man in toll-collector grey crouches behind the counter. He's bleeding. He's armed. He's staring at you like you might be the fourth person today come to kill him for something he found in his own cellar.
authorOnlyNotes: Orvyn found the ledger three days ago during a repair in the cellar — it was hidden in a sealed compartment.
He tried to sell information about it to the Compact and they sent soldiers instead of coin.
He does not know that the ledger also has his own name in it — he is listed as a paid informant from twelve years ago. Surface this in the Reveal beat.
content.stakes: Orvyn is the only character who can tell the player what is in the cellar and why three factions want it. If he dies or flees, the player loses critical context.
entryConditions: Player has entered the tollhouse interior
exitConditions: orvyn_trust_level is set to any value
stateChanges: Sets: orvyn_trust_level = [closed | partial | full] based on dialogue path taken
Sets: orvyn_healed = true (if player uses healing item or skill on Orvyn)

Orvyn Kett NPC — wounded state (bolt in shoulder), crossbow drawn, crouching animation
Healing interaction prompt — context-sensitive, appears when player has healing item/skill equipped
Dialogue tree — three branches: aggressive (closes off after 2 exchanges), neutral (partial info), empathetic (full info)
Orvyn wound visual: bolt in shoulder, blood staining on uniform

annotations.text: His name is in the ledger. Do not surface this in his dialogue — it lands best as the Reveal beat's key moment.
He smells like pipe smoke and old fear. He has been here for decades. The tollhouse is his entire life.

frames.title: Who Do You Trust?
frames.summary: Three factions want the ledger. Each sends a representative. The player must decide who — if anyone — to deal with, or whether to keep the ledger themselves.

content.designerNotes: The three factions arrive within the same short window — design this as an escalating pressure sequence, not a clean negotiation screen. Compact agent is overt and threatening. Velthari courier is measured and strategic. Dalthor factor is desperate and overpays. Player can choose none — which accelerates the encounter beat.
content.playerVisibleText: Three people want what you found. One is a soldier with legal authority and a bad temper. One is a spy with coin and no emotion. One is a merchant representative who looks like they haven't slept in two days. They each say the ledger is theirs by right.
authorOnlyNotes: The Compact agent plans to arrest Orvyn regardless of the ledger outcome — he knows about Orvyn's old informant role.
The Velthari courier is not here to recover the ledger — she wants to copy it and let the original be destroyed, to keep the blackmail value private to Velthari.
The Dalthor factor knows the ledger implicates the Dalthor house in the war crimes. She is trying to destroy it before anyone reads it fully.
involvedCharacters: Preket (Compact military agent, aggressive, has legal backing)
Savan Vreil (Velthari intelligence courier, calm, dangerous)
Issa Dalthor (merchant house factor, desperate, hiding something)
content.stakes: The choice here determines which faction the player is now marked by — and which ones become opponents.
exitConditions: ledger_recipient is set OR negotiation_timer_expired = true
stateChanges: Sets: negotiation_timer_expired = true if player refuses all three or timer runs out
Updates: compact_faction_standing, velthari_faction_standing, dalthor_faction_standing based on choice

Pressure timer UI element (optional — recommend as ambient environmental pressure, not HUD timer)

annotations.text: All paths lead to the encounter beat — tension is already too high regardless of choice.
If the player reads the ledger during this beat, skip to the Reveal beat immediately.

frames.title: Ambush at the Tollhouse
frames.summary: The negotiation breaks down — or was never going to hold. Compact soldiers breach the perimeter. Velthari moves to extract the ledger. Dalthor's factor tries to burn it.

content.designerNotes: Design this as a three-way conflict, not a binary fight. The factions are as much threats to each other as to the player. The ledger itself is the objective — control it, protect it, or escape with it. Scale the encounter to the player's current resource state. This is a tense standoff that turns violent, not a dungeon clearance.
content.playerVisibleText: Boots outside. Savan breaks left toward the cellar. The Compact soldier draws steel. Issa Dalthor has a lamp and is moving toward the records shelf. The tollhouse is suddenly very small.
authorOnlyNotes: Savan's goal is to photograph/copy the ledger — not to kill anyone. She has materials for this.
The Compact soldiers will move to arrest Orvyn on sight. Protecting him splits player attention.
Issa will attempt to burn the ledger if cornered — she has too much to lose.
involvedCharacters: Orvyn Kett (needs protecting or will flee)
content.stakes: Who controls the ledger when the encounter ends determines which Consequence branch the player enters.
entryConditions: ledger_recipient is set OR negotiation_timer_expired = true
Player is in the tollhouse or exterior zone
stateChanges: Sets: savan_escaped = true (default unless player specifically blocks her path)

Savan Vreil scripted escape route — exit path from cellar hatch to treeline
Compact soldiers x3 spawn + Preket — combat-ready placement at front door
Issa Dalthor with lamp — fire hazard interaction trigger at records shelf
Orvyn Kett NPC protection trigger — aggros Compact soldiers if player ignores him
Ledger pickup object — physics-enabled, interactable, visually distinct
testCriteria: encounter_outcome is set on combat resolution regardless of which path player takes

implementationChecklist: Design the tollhouse combat space: cellar hatch, front door, one window — three faction entry points
Implement Savan's escape route — she should exit unless the player specifically intercepts
Scale Compact soldier count to player level or current resource state

annotations.text: Savan escaping with a partial copy is the setup for the Future Thread frame. Do not kill her by default.
Target 15–25 minutes of play time. Keep pressure on. The Reveal lands best when the player is still catching their breath.

frames.title: What the Ledger Actually Says
frames.summary: The player reads the ledger. It lists payments, names, and dates spanning twelve years of a regional war — including names the player recognizes, and one name they didn't expect.

content.designerNotes: Surface three specific ledger entries through an in-engine readable document — names of dead villages, payments to commanders, supply diversions. Then surface Orvyn's name. Hold on it. The ledger also contains at least one name from the player's prior quest history if applicable — implement a contextual slot for this.
content.playerVisibleText: The ledger is not just accounts. It is a record of who paid whom to look the other way while three settlements burned. The Compact. The Velthari Compact's regional liaison. And the Dalthor house, who supplied the food chain that was quietly cut. And near the bottom of page eleven: the name of the old man bleeding on the floor behind you.
authorOnlyNotes: Orvyn was a paid informant — he reported on road travelers for coin. He did not know what it was funding.
One entry is redacted. Someone already tore a page. That page named a fourth party never mentioned.
The ledger proves war crimes but cannot be used as legal evidence in the Compact's courts without the missing page.
content.stakes: The player now knows the full weight of what they are holding. Every choice from here carries moral consequence.
stateChanges: Unlocks: consequence-expose and consequence-conceal (both branches now available)

Orvyn reaction scripted sequence — shame response, triggered on ledger_contents_known becoming true

Contextual slot for prior-quest name (if applicable to campaign continuity)

annotations.text: The missing page is the next quest's thread. Do not answer it here — leave it explicitly open.
The ink is old. The handwriting on Orvyn's entry is different from the rest — added later, by a different hand.

frames.title: Consequence A: The Ledger Goes Public
frames.summary: The player delivers or releases the ledger. The Compact scrambles. The Dalthor house loses its road charter. Orvyn is arrested. The region shifts.

content.designerNotes: This is not a clean victory. The Compact tries to spin the ledger as a forgery. The Dalthor house collapses within the week — but the roads they ran go dark. Orvyn is taken. The region is destabilized. Velthari thanks the player quietly and files the event. Surface all of this through world-state changes in subsequent quests.
content.playerVisibleText: The ledger's contents spread faster than anyone expected. By the time the Compact tries to suppress it, three town criers have already read it aloud in the Ashmarrow market. The Dalthor trade routes shut overnight. The roads are now unwatched.
authorOnlyNotes: Velthari already had a copy thanks to Savan. The public ledger serves their interests — they encouraged its release through a third party.
The Compact's internal investigation will eventually reach the player — design this for Quest 03 or later.
content.stakes: The player has destabilized the region. The roads are dangerous now.

annotations.text: Leads to Future Thread. Savan is gone with a partial copy — that thread stays open regardless.

frames.title: Consequence B: The Ledger Is Hidden or Sold
frames.summary: The player sells, trades, or conceals the ledger. The crimes stay buried. The factions get what they wanted. The player has made enemies of whoever didn't get it.

content.designerNotes: This is a morally heavier outcome than it appears. The Compact keeps its reputation. The Dalthor routes reopen. Orvyn is quietly released. But nothing has changed — the people in the ledger are still in power. Design subsequent quests to surface this weight in a later chapter.
content.playerVisibleText: The ledger disappears into the right hands. Within days, the tollhouse is quietly repaired. Orvyn is walking free. The road through Ashmarrow Pass is as busy as it always was. As if nothing happened.
authorOnlyNotes: Savan still has her partial copy. She will use it eventually, on a timeline the designer controls.
The faction that received the ledger now has leverage over the player — they know the player can be bought.
content.stakes: The player has chosen stability over accountability. That choice has a weight that will return.

frames.title: Savan Has a Copy
frames.summary: Velthari intelligence courier Savan Vreil escaped the tollhouse with a transcribed partial copy of the ledger. She will use it. The player doesn't know when.

content.designerNotes: This frame closes the quest but opens the next thread. Savan is not an antagonist — she is a professional who did her job. She may contact the player again as an employer, a warning, or a source. The copy she made is incomplete (she was interrupted) but it names enough to be dangerous. Reserve this for Quest 02 or a later chapter.
content.playerVisibleText: Three days after the tollhouse, a folded note arrives at wherever the player is resting. No seal. No signature. One line: 'The copy I made is incomplete. I may need what you remember. — S'
authorOnlyNotes: Savan's copy is missing the entries for pages 7–9 — which cover the Compact's regional liaison by name.
She is not working against the player. She is working on a longer timeline.
If the player exposed the ledger, Savan is pleased. If they buried it, she is patient.
involvedCharacters: Savan Vreil (Velthari courier, now a recurring contact)
content.stakes: An intentionally open thread. Savan will matter in a future quest.

Deliver as an epilogue beat after the consequence plays out. End on the question, not the answer.
